In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the peak to valley current ratio (PVCR) of the RTD can be enhanced by optimizing the well width, barrier thickness, and spacer layer thickness.

the optimum spacer layer is half of the de Broglie wavelength associated to the bound state of finite quantum well, the optimum well width is 3 times of the de Brogile wavelength associated with the ground state of the corresponding well and the optimum barrier thickness is 3.5 times of the de-Brogile wavelength of the bound state in the barrier.
the proposed relations for the optimal well width and barrier width are valid for any RTD based on appropriate materials.

we have proposed the optimum values for well and barrier width and spacer width to achieve the highest peak to valley current ratio in RTD.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the optimum well and barrier width and the optimum spacer width are independent of the doping concentration.
the PVCR of the RTD can be increased by increasing the well width and barrier width and decreasing the spacer layer width.
